FRAMING CORRECTED, scope INCREASED, priority unchanged. From the wordfeatures engineer via the owner, confirmed by me against source.

My original wording -- 'PERFECT SENSORY AGREEMENT', 'agrees perfectly with every node' -- overstates it. dSens sits in an ADDITIVE cost where zero is the neutral minimum contribution, so an empty unit is not rewarded. The precise defect is an ASYMMETRY: a sensory-rich unit can be penalised whenever lexical coverage misses; an empty unit cannot be penalised at all; and nothing in the result records which case occurred.

The scientific risk, sharper than my original statement: this can confound groups differing in RECALL VIVIDNESS. A group producing sensorimotor-rich recall is exposed to a penalty channel a group producing vague recall is not -- a between-group artefact in a library built for comparing recall.

SCOPE INCREASE: this is a WIRE FORMAT change, not only a cost change. wire.scala:183 sets OptionalTerms = Set(CostTerm.Chart, CostTerm.Structural), so Sensory can never be recorded missing. Fixing the arithmetic alone leaves a format that still cannot express the difference between no evidence and a perfect match.

MAGNITUDE, so nobody over-reads it: default sensory weight is 0.15 (CostWeights.default = unsafe(1.0, 0.5, 0.4, 0.15, 0.3, 1.0)). Real defect, low-weighted term, worth fixing correctly and not an emergency.
